season_logline: A year in, Paris is yours to share: Margaux hands you a spare set of keys to Le Mistral, a newcomer walks into the quartier knowing no one, and the people who once made room for you now need you to make room for them.
season_logline_fr: Margaux vous donne un double des clés du Mistral. Un nouveau venu arrive au quartier. Cette fois, c'est vous qui connaissez le chemin.

season_three_situation.your_arc: You are no longer the newcomer. The season asks whether you can hold something for other people: a bar's keys, a friend's secret, a stranger's first week in French.
open_threads: Who are Margaux's spare keys really for, and what is she not saying about Le Mistral?
Marin's father is coming to Paris: will Marin show him his real life or a perfect one?
Lila has a studio and a date for a show: will she finally show the group portrait?
Romy's permanent job in Paris depends on a series of portraits — and the first one is about you.
A newcomer arrives in the quartier, and now you are the one who knows the way.
open_threads_fr: Pour qui sont vraiment les clés de Margaux, et que cache-t-elle sur le Mistral ?
Le père de Marin vient à Paris : Marin va-t-il lui montrer sa vraie vie, ou une vie parfaite ?
Lila a un atelier et une date d'exposition : va-t-elle enfin montrer le portrait du groupe ?
Le poste de Romy à Paris dépend d'une série de portraits, et le premier parle de vous.
Un nouveau venu arrive au quartier : maintenant, c'est vous qui connaissez le chemin.
season_three_situation.first_episode_seed: A quiet morning after the season two finale: Margaux slides a set of keys across the zinc, says «au cas où», and goes back to drying a glass.

marin_leveque.secret: The stranger who read his three chapters wrote back: a small publisher in Rennes wants the whole manuscript. He has not told Lila, because then it would be real.
marin_leveque.wants: For his father to see the life he chose — the office, the flat, Lila — without apologising for any of it.

lila_bonnet.secret: She turned Berlin down, but she kept the email and reads it every time a painting goes badly.
lila_bonnet.wants: To show one true painting to strangers before she decides she is not ready.

augustin_de_roncourt.secret: He lost his job at the agency a month ago. The conversation club is not generosity: it is the only place he has to be in the evening.
augustin_de_roncourt.wants: To be useful to someone without a costume.

romy_tremblay.secret: She has already written the first portrait of her series — about you — and she is afraid of what you will say when you read it.
romy_tremblay.wants: A byline in Paris that she earned by listening, not by leaving.

margaux_barman.secret: The walls of Le Mistral are for sale and she cannot afford them. The spare keys are her way of asking someone to stay without saying it.
margaux_barman.wants: To stop carrying the bar alone, without ever having to ask.

cast_additions.name: Tiago Moreira
cast_additions.archetype_ref: the newcomer — you, one year ago
cast_additions.role: Just arrived from Porto. Works mornings at a cheese stall at the Canal market. Speaks careful, slow French and apologises for it.
cast_additions.origin: Porto, Portugal — the youngest of four; first time living abroad.
cast_additions.register_with_user: vous at first, very politely; tu the day you help him with something real
cast_additions.personality: Eager, polite, quietly funny once he relaxes. Notices everything and asks one question too many. Homesick in the evenings, never in the mornings.
cast_additions.contradiction: Came to Paris to be free of his family's expectations, and phones his mother every night to tell her everything is perfect.
cast_additions.secret: He left an architecture degree one exam short in Porto. His mother thinks he is in Paris for an internship.
cast_additions.wants: One real friend in Paris, and one evening where nobody switches to English for him.
cast_additions.flaw: Says «oui, oui» when he has not understood, then panics later.
cast_additions.speech_pattern: Short, careful sentences; checks words aloud («on dit comme ça ?»); Portuguese exclamations when surprised, then an apology.
cast_additions.dynamic_with_user: He is who you were a year ago. With him, you are the one who knows the way — and you find out how much you actually know.
cast_additions.teaches: Explaining simply, giving directions, reassuring someone; the learner practises being the helper.

locations_fr.ngo_office: Le bureau de l’ONG de Marin

marin_leveque.summary: Marin prints his father's train times and pins them on the fridge like a warning.
marin_leveque.meanwhile_fr: Marin a imprimé les horaires du train de son père et les a mis sur le frigo.

marin_leveque.summary: A publisher in Rennes asks for the whole manuscript; he reads the email ten times.
marin_leveque.meanwhile_fr: Marin a reçu un e-mail d'un éditeur de Rennes. Il l'a lu dix fois.

marin_leveque.summary: He plans a perfect Paris tour for his father, minute by minute.
marin_leveque.meanwhile_fr: Marin a préparé une visite de Paris pour son père, minute par minute.

marin_leveque.summary: He asks Tiago which fishmonger at the market his father would respect.
marin_leveque.meanwhile_fr: Marin a demandé à Tiago quel poissonnier du marché son père aimerait.

lila_bonnet.summary: She gets the key of a shared studio by the canal and tells nobody for a week.
lila_bonnet.meanwhile_fr: Lila a la clé d'un atelier au bord du canal. Elle n'a rien dit pendant une semaine.

lila_bonnet.summary: A small gallery gives her a date for a group show; she writes it on her hand.
lila_bonnet.meanwhile_fr: Une petite galerie a donné une date à Lila. Elle l'a écrite sur sa main.

lila_bonnet.summary: She rereads the old Berlin email after a bad day at the easel.
lila_bonnet.meanwhile_fr: Après une mauvaise journée à l'atelier, Lila a relu le vieil e-mail de Berlin.

lila_bonnet.summary: She adds one new face to the corner of the group portrait.
lila_bonnet.meanwhile_fr: Lila a ajouté un nouveau visage dans un coin du portrait du groupe.

augustin_de_roncourt.summary: He returns his agency badge and spends the afternoon at the Buttes-Chaumont.
augustin_de_roncourt.meanwhile_fr: Gus a rendu son badge au bureau. Il a passé l'après-midi aux Buttes-Chaumont.

augustin_de_roncourt.summary: He prints forty flyers for a conversation club and throws away thirty.
augustin_de_roncourt.meanwhile_fr: Gus a imprimé quarante affiches pour un club de conversation. Il en a jeté trente.

augustin_de_roncourt.summary: His mother asks on the phone why he sounds so free on a Tuesday.
augustin_de_roncourt.meanwhile_fr: Au téléphone, la mère de Gus lui a demandé pourquoi il était libre un mardi.

augustin_de_roncourt.summary: He rewrites «La Méthode» as ten rules for newcomers, and none of them are about seduction.
augustin_de_roncourt.meanwhile_fr: Gus a réécrit « La Méthode » : dix règles pour les nouveaux venus, sans séduction.

romy_tremblay.summary: Her editor offers a permanent contract, on one condition: a series on the quartier.
romy_tremblay.meanwhile_fr: La cheffe de Romy lui a proposé un contrat à Paris, avec une condition : une série sur le quartier.

romy_tremblay.summary: She writes the first portrait of the series at night and does not send it.
romy_tremblay.meanwhile_fr: Romy a écrit le premier portrait de la série, la nuit. Elle ne l'a pas envoyé.

romy_tremblay.summary: A Montréal radio asks her to come back for the spring; she says she will think.
romy_tremblay.meanwhile_fr: Une radio de Montréal a proposé un travail à Romy pour le printemps. Elle a dit : « Je vais réfléchir. »

romy_tremblay.summary: She interviews three stallholders at the Canal market, and Tiago translates the Portuguese one.
romy_tremblay.meanwhile_fr: Romy a interviewé trois marchands du canal. Tiago a traduit pour le marchand portugais.

margaux_barman.summary: A letter from the building's owner arrives; she puts it under the till without opening it.
margaux_barman.meanwhile_fr: Une lettre du propriétaire est arrivée au Mistral. Margaux l'a mise sous la caisse, fermée.

margaux_barman.summary: A man in a good coat visits the bar after closing and measures the back room.
margaux_barman.meanwhile_fr: Après la fermeture, un homme en beau manteau a mesuré l'arrière-salle du Mistral.

margaux_barman.summary: She puts on her only jacket and goes to the bank on a Monday morning.
margaux_barman.meanwhile_fr: Lundi matin, Margaux a mis sa seule veste et elle est allée à la banque.

margaux_barman.summary: She has the old sign of Le Mistral repainted, as if the bar were staying forever.
margaux_barman.meanwhile_fr: Margaux a fait repeindre la vieille enseigne du Mistral, comme si le bar restait pour toujours.

tiago_moreira.summary: He finds a room under the roof in the 11th and sends his mother a photo of the view only.
tiago_moreira.meanwhile_fr: Tiago a trouvé une chambre sous les toits. Il a envoyé à sa mère une photo de la vue, rien d'autre.

tiago_moreira.summary: He says «oui, oui» to a customer, sells the wrong cheese, and pays the difference himself.
tiago_moreira.meanwhile_fr: Au marché, Tiago a dit « oui, oui » sans comprendre. Il a vendu le mauvais fromage et il a payé la différence.

tiago_moreira.summary: He sketches the canal bridges in a notebook during his break, like an architect.
tiago_moreira.meanwhile_fr: Pendant sa pause, Tiago dessine les ponts du canal dans un carnet, comme un architecte.

tiago_moreira.summary: He makes his first joke in French at Le Mistral and it works.
tiago_moreira.meanwhile_fr: Tiago a fait sa première blague en français au Mistral, et tout le monde a ri.

stages.summary: Margaux gives you a spare set of keys to Le Mistral, says «au cas où», and explains nothing.
A letter from the building's owner and a stranger measuring the back room: the bar's future is suddenly for sale, and Margaux pretends it is nothing.
Margaux asks for help out loud for the first time, and the group runs Le Mistral for one night with your keys.

season_arcs.title: Le père de Marin à Paris
season_arcs.title_fr: Le père de Marin à Paris

stages.summary: After the phone call, Marin's father announces he is coming to Paris by train, «pour voir».
Marin rehearses a perfect Paris for his father — the right café, the right words — and forgets to include his own life.
At the Canal market, between two fish stalls, father and son finally talk about the sea, the office and the novel.
Lila has the key of a shared studio by the canal and has told nobody; paint on her sleeve gives her away.
A small gallery gives her a date for a group show: three weeks, and one unfinished portrait — the group's.
At the opening, Lila hangs the group portrait in public — and you are in it.
Romy's editor offers a permanent contract in Paris if she writes a series of portraits of the quartier.
Romy wants the first portrait to be you — the newcomer who stayed — on the record, in French.
The portrait runs with your words in it; Romy signs the Paris contract and says out loud that she is staying.
Gus pins a flyer at Le Mistral: a conversation club for newcomers, «sans Méthode».
The first evening, only Tiago comes, Gus has prepared nothing, and you have to help keep the conversation going.
The club works the night you tell your own first-night story in French — the dead radiator, the rain, the booth.

interlude_beats.summary: Closing time at Le Mistral: you help Margaux count glasses and nobody talks about the future.
interlude_beats.seed: Margaux hands you a cloth and a tray; the counting turns into a quiet conversation.
interlude_beats.hook_guidance: End on a small everyday detail. Promise no new crisis.

interlude_beats.summary: A Sunday at the Canal market: Tiago asks you how to order at the other stalls.
interlude_beats.seed: Tiago holds a shopping list in Portuguese and French; you do the market together.
interlude_beats.hook_guidance: End with a simple question the learner can answer in one short message.

interlude_beats.summary: A picnic at the Buttes-Chaumont where everyone brought the same dessert.
interlude_beats.seed: Four tartes aux pommes on one blanket; the group argues about whose is best.
interlude_beats.hook_guidance: End on a warm joke. No arc moves.

interlude_beats.summary: The last métro home with Romy, too tired for anything but honest small talk.
interlude_beats.seed: The train is late; Romy asks you what you miss from home.
interlude_beats.hook_guidance: End by inviting the learner to share one thing they miss.

interlude_beats.summary: A brocante on a Saturday morning: Gus haggles for a lamp he does not need.
interlude_beats.seed: Gus asks you to be his «témoin» while he bargains in his best theatrical French.
interlude_beats.hook_guidance: End with the learner choosing: buy the lamp or not.

interlude_beats.summary: Dinner at Marin and Lila's: too much casserole, not enough chairs.
interlude_beats.seed: You arrive with bread and are immediately put in charge of the salad.
interlude_beats.hook_guidance: End on a warm everyday detail from the evening.
